To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the presence of dynamic data makes the distribution of XML data more challenging, (ii) the cost of a dynamic XML query is not simply the cost of evaluating the static part of the query, but also depends on the cost of the service calls, which in turn depend on the location of the services, and (iii) the replication of dynamic XML documents is a complex problem that requires a careful analysis of the cost of maintaining and querying the data.

the distribution and replication problem for dynamic XML documents can be solved in the same way as for regular XML documents, but that the cost model for dynamic XML queries is more complex than for regular XML queries, and that the cost model can be used in a distributed and replicated environment to decide which data and services should be replicated at which peer.

(a) a cost model is needed to determine which dynamic XML documents to replicate and where to replicate them, and (b) the cost model should be able to capture the impact of service calls on query processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) how can we evaluate queries over distributed and/or replicated dynamic data, (2) what is the cost of evaluating such queries, and (3) how to replicate data and services to optimize the cost of query execution.

the following aspects of dynamic data: (i) a data model and query language that support the dynamic data; (ii) a distributed and replicated storage model; (iii) an efficient cost model; (iv) a query optimization algorithm.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

dynamic XML data, and in particular Active XML documents, raise many new issues for the design of distributed systems, which we hope will stimulate the development of new distributed systems that can efficiently support these new data models and query languages.

the Active XML system provides a framework for dynamic data that is both expressive and efficient, with a clear separation between the data model, the query language, the cost model, the replication and distribution algorithms and the query execution engine.
we have shown how to make the Active XML system scale to a very large number of nodes, and how to make the system robust to node failures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Active XML model, which was originally conceived to support dynamic XML documents, is a good basis for the design of dynamic XML documents that can be distributed and replicated.
the distribution and replication techniques for dynamic XML data that we propose in this paper are a natural extension of the techniques used for regular XML data.
we provide a complete framework for the management of distributed and replicated dynamic documents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when dealing with dynamic XML documents, the cost model for query execution is much more involved than in the traditional case.
the distribution and replication issues raised by dynamic XML documents are quite different from those of regular XML data.
, while the distribution and replication issues for dynamic XML data are more difficult than for static XML data, they are also more interesting.
